title: How Vaccination Works
learning_objective: Vaccination helps train the immune system to recognize specific infections, reducing the risk of severe disease and community spread.

sections.heading: Core concepts
sections.content: Vaccines introduce weakened or inactive pathogens into the body, prompting the immune system to produce antibodies. This prepares the body to fight off the actual infection if encountered later.

sections.heading: Practical guidance
sections.content: Consult your local public health authority or a qualified healthcare professional for a vaccination schedule tailored to your age, health status, and vaccine history.

sections.heading: What to observe or ask
sections.content: Some vaccines can cause temporary side effects like soreness or mild fever. If you experience severe symptoms or have concerns, contact a healthcare professional immediately.

sections.heading: When to seek help
sections.content: Seek emergency care for severe or life-threatening symptoms. Consult a qualified healthcare professional for personalized advice and reassurance.

title: Why Vaccination Matters
learning_objective: Vaccination helps train the immune system to recognize specific infections, reducing the risk of severe disease and community spread.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies against specific pathogens, providing long-lasting immunity without causing disease. This reduces the risk of severe illness and protects against outbreaks.

sections.heading: Practical Guidance
sections.content: Consult your local public health authority or a qualified healthcare professional for a personalized vaccination schedule. This ensures the most up-to-date and appropriate vaccines for your age, health status, and vaccine history.

sections.heading: What to Observe or Ask
sections.content: Some vaccines may cause mild side effects like soreness or a low-grade fever. If you experience severe symptoms or have concerns, contact your healthcare provider immediately.

sections.heading: When to Seek Help
sections.content: If you have severe or life-threatening symptoms after vaccination, seek emergency care. This includes symptoms such as difficulty breathing, persistent high fever, or signs of severe allergic reactions.

title: Common Side Effects and Safety of Vaccinations
learning_objective: Vaccinations are crucial for building immunity against diseases. They can cause mild side effects like soreness or fever, but these are usually short-lived. Always consult a healthcare professional for specific advice.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Vaccinations train the immune system to recognize specific infections, reducing the risk of severe disease and community spread. They are essential for public health.

sections.heading: Practical Guidance
sections.content: Vaccines can cause temporary side effects such as soreness or mild fever. These are usually mild and resolve within a few days. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

sections.heading: What to Observe or Ask
sections.content: Some vaccines can cause mild side effects. Ask your healthcare provider about individual risks and symptoms. If you experience severe reactions, seek immediate medical attention.

sections.heading: When to Seek Help
sections.content: If you experience severe reactions such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or lips, or a high fever, seek emergency care immediately. These could be signs of an allergic reaction or other severe side effects.
